name: 追金骑
The Gold Hunters
before: 戈壁上卷起一溜黄尘，一大队金面骑卫在沙丘间来回搜，步卒拿长杆一路戳沙堆，骑卫在前头堵口子。他们在找一个人，见了谁都要掀开领子看看。你们的驼队刚翻过沙梁，就被他们团团围住：「领子里藏没藏金子？」

A line of yellow dust rolls across the gravel desert: a big company of Gold Mask riders sweeping back and forth among the dunes, foot soldiers prodding every sand heap with long poles, riders blocking the gaps ahead. They're looking for someone, and they turn back the collar of everyone they meet. Your camels have barely crested the ridge when they surround you. 'Any gold hidden in your collars?'
after: 骑卫们被打退，领头的丢下一本小册子，是金面卫追金的账：「刮金七人，已获其六。追回金一钱，尚欠二分，在第七人处。」底下画着一个十二三岁的孩子的模样。七年了，洞主一分一厘地追，就差这最后两分。

The riders beaten off, their leader drops a little book: the Gold Masks' tally of the hunt. 'Seven gold scrapers, six taken. One tenth of an ounce recovered. Two hundredths still owed, held by the seventh man.' Below is a sketch of a boy of twelve or thirteen. Seven years the Lord has hunted it down grain by grain, and only these last two hundredths are missing.

name: 七旗卡
Seven Banners Post
before: 上山的大路口立着一道卡子，卡墙上插着七面旗，旗上都写着一个大大的「千」字，有的崭新，有的已经褪了色。守卡的金面刀卫看见你们的旗，冷笑一声：「又来一个。第八面。」刀卫和弩手一齐压了上来。

A checkpoint stands where the main road turns up the mountain, and on its wall are planted seven banners, each bearing a great character Qian, some brand new, some faded. The Gold Mask swordsmen on guard see your banner and laugh coldly. 'Another one. Number eight.' Swords and crossbows close in together.
after: 刀卫们被打退，卡官领你们看那七面旗：一面是关内商号的，想冒认千里号的买卖；一面是盗经贼的，想混进窟里；一面是个骗子的，说自己是账房的儿子……七拨人都说是千里号的后来者。「洞主见一个信一回，被骗一回，」卡官说，「到第五拨，就谁也不信了。」

The swordsmen beaten back, the post officer shows you the seven banners. One came from a merchant house inside the Pass that wanted to claim the Qianli caravan's trade. One from sutra thieves who wanted to slip into the caves. One from a swindler claiming to be the bookkeeper's son. All seven said they were the ones who came after. 'Each time, the Lord believed, and each time he was fooled,' says the officer. 'By the fifth he stopped believing anyone.'

name: 铜面营
Bronze Mask Camp
before: 河边扎着一大营金面卫，营里的人跟别处不一样：脸上戴的不是金面，是铜面，铜面上还刻着一个数，从一刻到六。他们守着河边的渡口，不许任何人往山上运东西，打起来却不要命，好像在跟谁赎罪。

A big Gold Mask camp sits by the river, but these men are different: they wear bronze masks, not gold, each engraved with a number from one to six. They hold the river crossing and let no cargo through toward the mountain, and when they fight they hold nothing back, as if paying off a debt to someone.
after: 铜面卫被打退，戴「一」的那个摘下面具，是个满脸褶子的中年人。他说他们六个就是当年刮千里窟的刮金帮，被洞主一个个抓了回来。洞主没杀他们，叫他们戴上铜面守窟，「戴着这张脸，就记得自己刮过谁的脸」。他望着戈壁：「第七个还小，那年才十二。」

The bronze masks beaten back, number one takes his off: a middle-aged man with a deeply lined face. The six of them, he says, are the Gold Scrapers who scraped the Qianli Cave, caught one by one by the Lord. He didn't kill them; he masked them in bronze and set them to guard the caves. 'Wear this face and you'll remember whose faces you scraped.' He looks out over the desert. 'The seventh was only a kid. Twelve, that year.'

name: 阿七村
A-Qi's Village
before: 河边一个小村，村口的柳树下拴着几条船。一伙河霸占了村里的渡船，过河一人十钱，交不起的就扣下牲口。村里一个老汉被他们推进了河里，爬上来还在念叨：「阿七他娘的坟，还在对岸呢……」

A little village by the river, boats tied under the willow at its edge. River bullies have seized the village ferry, ten coins a head to cross, and those who can't pay have their animals taken. They've shoved an old man into the river, and when he crawls out he's still muttering: 'A-Qi's mother's grave is still on the other bank...'
after: 河霸被赶走，老汉把船撑过去，领你们看对岸的一座小坟。他说阿七七年前跟着一伙坏人跑了一趟千佛洞，回来就像丢了魂，再不肯碰金子。去年冬天他娘死了，他埋了娘，去给驼队拉骆驼，「临走在坟前跪了一夜，说娘，我欠的那一笔，我去还」。

The bullies chased off, the old man poles the ferry across and shows you a small grave on the far side. Seven years ago, he says, A-Qi went to the caves once with a bad crowd and came back like a lost soul, and never touched gold again. His mother died last winter. He buried her and went off to lead camels for a caravan. 'He knelt at her grave all night before he left and said, Mother, the debt I owe, I'm going to pay it.'

name: 晒经滩
Sutra Drying Strand
before: 河滩上铺满了经卷，一卷一卷摊开晒着，几个老和尚跪在边上，用扇子轻轻地扇。上游一个窟前几天渗了水，一窟的经都湿了，金面卫连夜一卷卷背下来晒。可滩边埋伏着一伙盗经贼，等太阳偏西、和尚们收经的时候下手。

The riverbank is spread with sutra scrolls laid open to dry, and old monks kneel among them fanning gently. A few days ago water seeped into a cave upstream and soaked every scroll in it; the Gold Masks carried them down through the night to dry. But sutra thieves lie in wait at the edge of the strand, ready to strike when the sun dips and the monks begin rolling them up.
after: 盗经贼被打跑，经卷一卷没少。一个金面卫一边帮着收经一边说，那天夜里窟里进水，洞主第一个冲了进去，抱着经卷往外跑，脚下一滑掉进了河里，「洞主不会水，扑腾着也不撒手」。老和尚笑了：「他小时候在粥棚烧火，就这样，锅翻了也不撒勺子。」

The thieves chased off, not a scroll is lost. One of the Gold Masks, helping roll them up, says that the night the water came in, the Lord was first into the cave, running out with armfuls of scrolls, and slipped into the river. 'The Lord can't swim. He thrashed about and still wouldn't let go.' An old monk laughs. 'Same as when he tended the fire at the porridge shed as a boy. Pot tipped over, still wouldn't let go of the ladle.'

name: 金秤市
The Gold Scale Market
before: 戈壁边上一座小集，是千佛洞方圆几百里买卖金子的地方：修窟要贴金，画匠要金粉，崖上凿出来的好石料也拿来这儿换金。洞主有令，集上所有的金子只许卖给金面卫，一分一厘都要过他们的秤。如今一伙沙匪看准了这条规矩，劫了金面卫的秤台，自己当起了「金面」，见金就收，见人就宰。

A little market at the edge of the desert, where all the gold within a few hundred miles of the caves is bought and sold: gilding for the caves, gold dust for painters, and the fine stone cut from the cliff comes here to be traded for gold. By the Lord's order every grain of gold in the market may be sold only to the Gold Masks, weighed on their scale. A gang of sand bandits has seen its chance, seized the Gold Masks' scale platform and set themselves up as the 'Gold Masks', taking every scrap of gold and fleecing everyone.
after: 沙匪被赶走，金秤市重新开了张：崖上的石料一车车拉来，换走金子，买卖又热闹起来。管秤的老头说，洞主收金，不是为了自己发财，是一分一分地凑：「他说欠了三百个人一钱二分金，要一分不少地还回去。」上个月有个拉骆驼的年轻人来问过他，怎么把一点金子还给寺里，又不让人知道是谁还的。老头说：「我告诉他，最好的法子，是当面还。」

The sand bandits driven off, the market opens again: stone from the cliff comes in by the cartload and leaves as gold, and trade is lively once more. The old man who keeps the scale says the Lord buys gold not to get rich but to make up a sum, grain by grain. 'He says he owes three hundred people one tenth of an ounce and a little more, and he'll pay back every grain.' Last month a young camel driver came asking how to give a little gold back to the temple without anyone knowing who gave it. 'I told him,' says the old man, 'the best way is to pay it back face to face.'

name: 销赃帐
The Fence's Tent
before: 沙窝里一顶油布大帐，是盗经贼的销赃铺，帐里挂着一卷卷经，每卷底下吊着一块价牌，最贵的一卷标着「千里经，五卷一套，不拆卖」。帐外一伙打手正在验货，一个买主已经掏出了银子。了账一看那几卷经的铜轴，就扑了上去。

In a sandy hollow stands a big oilcloth tent: the sutra thieves' fence. Inside hang scroll after scroll, a price tag dangling from each, and the dearest reads 'Qianli Sutra, set of five, not sold separately'. Outside, toughs are checking the goods, and a buyer has already brought out his silver. Liaozhang sees the bronze rollers on those scrolls and throws himself at them.
after: 打手和买主都跑了，五卷千里经被抢了回来。第五卷的末尾，是账房的字：「借寺中经一部，携往王城；抄经一部留寺，以为抵押。字丑，佛莫笑。愿此路平。」了账念完，把经卷贴在胸口：「他借走一部，还了一部，还多附了三百个人的字。」还差最后几卷。

Toughs and buyer both run, and five fascicles of the Qianli Sutra are recovered. At the end of the fifth is the bookkeeper's hand: 'One sutra borrowed from the temple, taken to the King's city. One sutra copied and left with the temple as surety. The handwriting is ugly; Buddha, don't laugh. May this road be smooth.' Liaozhang reads it aloud and presses the scroll to his chest. 'He borrowed one and gave one back, with three hundred people's handwriting thrown in.' The last few fascicles are still missing.

name: 攻崖营
Siege Camp
before: 草滩上扎着一座大营，营里堆着云梯、绳钩、撬棍，一伙关内的雇佣兵正在操练攀崖，步、弩、骑都有。他们的头领拿着一张千佛洞的崖图，用朱笔圈了十几个窟：「哪个窟里有经、有画、有金，都在这儿了。」

A big camp stands on the grassland, heaped with scaling ladders, grappling hooks and crowbars, where mercenaries from inside the Pass, foot, crossbow and horse, are drilling cliff assaults. Their captain holds a plan of the caves with a dozen circled in red. 'Which caves have sutras, which have paintings, which have gold: it's all here.'
after: 雇佣兵被打散，你们在头领的帐里搜出一张契：「千佛洞内经卷壁画，得者与东家对半。」东家是关内一个大商号。你们这才明白，洞主闭山十年、养着一营金面卫，防的不是一两个小贼，是一个个这样的营盘。

The mercenaries scattered, you find a contract in the captain's tent: 'All sutras and murals taken from the caves to be split half and half with the patron.' The patron is a great merchant house inside the Pass. Now you understand: the Lord closed the mountain for ten years and kept a camp of Gold Masks not against the odd petty thief, but against camps like this, one after another.

name: 拉驼郎
The Camel Boy
before: 一支小驼队被一伙盗经贼截在路上，盗经贼要驼队帮他们驮赃，不驮就把骆驼宰了。拉头驼的是个十八九岁的小伙子，瘦得像根柴，一只手死死按着自己的衣领，另一只手攥着一根赶驼棍，挡在骆驼前面。

A small camel train has been stopped on the road by sutra thieves, who want it to carry their loot or they'll butcher the camels. The lead camel's driver is a lad of eighteen or nineteen, thin as a stick, one hand clamped to his collar, the other gripping a camel stick, standing in front of his animals.
after: 盗经贼被打跑，小伙子腿一软坐在地上。他就是阿七，当年刮金帮里最小的一个。他拆开衣领，里面缝着一个小纸包，是他分到的两分金粉，七年一粒没动。「我那年十二，就记得窟里三百张脸看着我，」他说，「想还，又怕金面，怕了七年。」他求你们带他上山。

The thieves chased off, the lad's legs give way and he sits down hard. He is A-Qi, youngest of the Gold Scrapers. He unpicks his collar: sewn inside is a tiny paper packet, his share of the gold dust, two hundredths of an ounce, untouched for seven years. 'I was twelve. All I remember is three hundred faces in the cave looking at me. I wanted to give it back, but I was scared of the Gold Mask. Seven years scared.' He begs you to take him up the mountain.

name: 背沙坡
Sand Basket Slope
before: 崖顶背后的沙坡上排着一溜香客，每人背一只筐，从窟顶上往下背沙。坡口的金面刀卫定了规矩：上山的人，先背一筐沙才许走。几个关内来的富商嫌脏，雇了打手要硬闯，跟刀卫打成一团，沙筐滚了一坡。

On the sand slope behind the clifftop, a line of pilgrims with baskets on their backs carries sand down off the cave roofs. The Gold Mask swordsmen at the head of the slope have made a rule: anyone going up the mountain must carry one basket of sand first. Some rich merchants from inside the Pass think it beneath them, hired toughs to force their way through, and are brawling with the guards, sand baskets rolling all over the slope.
after: 打手和刀卫都散了，你们拿起筐背沙。一个老香客说，沙压在窟顶上，下一场雨就渗下去，窟顶就塌，「洞主这条规矩，凶是凶，是给佛挡灾」。阿七一声不吭，背了十筐还不肯停，背到第十一筐，刀卫的头目拍了拍他的肩：「够了，小子，够了。」

Toughs and guards both dispersed, you take up baskets and carry sand. Sand left on a cave roof soaks through with the next rain and the roof collapses, an old pilgrim says. 'The Lord's rule is harsh, but it shields the Buddhas from harm.' A-Qi says nothing and carries ten baskets without stopping. As he shoulders the eleventh, the guard captain claps him on the shoulder. 'Enough, lad. That's enough.'

name: 盗经窝
Sutra Thieves' Warren
before: 沙里埋着半座废窟，窟口被盗经贼掏成了老鼠洞，一条条地道通到四面八方。千佛洞的经卷、关内收藏家的银子、过路的贼，都在这里进进出出。窝里的贼步、弩、骑都有，地道里还藏着暗哨。最里面的洞里，挂着千里经的最后几卷。

Half a ruined cave lies buried in the sand, its mouth burrowed by sutra thieves into a rat's nest of tunnels running every which way. Scrolls from the caves, silver from collectors inside the Pass and passing thieves all come and go through here. The thieves have foot, crossbow and horse, and sentries hidden in the tunnels. In the innermost chamber hang the last fascicles of the Qianli Sutra.
after: 这一窝贼被清了出去，千里经十卷凑齐了。最后一卷的末尾，三百个名字一个不少，最后一段经文却只抄了一半，下面一行小字：「此段账房抄，未毕，回程补。」了账说，账房欠的，又多了半段经。可千佛洞的经还在，关内的银子还在，盗经贼就杀不完；这一窝清了，过一阵，地道里又会钻进新的一窝。

This nest of thieves is cleared out and all ten fascicles of the Qianli Sutra are together again. At the end of the last, all three hundred names are there, but the final passage is only half copied, with a small note below: 'This section copied by the bookkeeper. Unfinished. To be completed on the way back.' The bookkeeper owes half a sutra more, says Liaozhang. But while the caves have scriptures and collectors inside the Pass have silver, there'll be no end of sutra thieves. Clear this nest and before long a new one will crawl into the tunnels.

name: 金面大营
The Gold Mask Camp
before: 戈壁上一座大营，营门两侧插满了旗，金面刀卫、弩手、骑卫列成三阵，面具在太阳底下连成一片金光，晃得人睁不开眼。这里是金面卫的老营，离洞主的山门只剩半天的路。营门口一个金面卫敲着铜锣，一声一声，像在数着什么。

A great camp on the gravel desert, banners thick on both sides of its gate, Gold Mask swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders drawn up in three formations, their masks joined into one blaze of gold in the sun that makes you squint. This is the Gold Masks' home camp, half a day from the Lord's gate. At the entrance a Gold Mask beats a bronze gong, stroke after stroke, as if counting.
after: 金面卫退回了山门，敲锣的那个说锣是每晚敲的，三百下，敲完了，洞主就提着一盏灯进千里窟，在三百个没有脸的人跟前坐到天亮。「十年了，一晚上都没落下。」他说洞主进窟以前，总要摘下金面挂在窟口，「他说在他们跟前，不能戴别人的脸」。

The Gold Masks fall back to the gate. The gong is struck every night, says the man who beats it, three hundred strokes. When they're done the Lord takes a lamp into the Qianli Cave and sits before the three hundred faceless figures until dawn. 'Ten years, and he's never missed a night.' Before he goes in he always takes off the golden mask and hangs it at the cave mouth. 'He says in front of them he can't wear someone else's face.'

name: 乱石扇
The Boulder Fan
before: 山口外铺开一大片扇形的碎石滩，滩上横七竖八全是干沟。金面卫在一条最宽的干沟里扎了个哨营，守着通往山门的小路，可小路在哪儿，外人谁也找不着。带路的老驼夫蹲下来看了看石头，脸色变了：「山里的云黑了，得赶紧把他们从沟里弄出来。」

Outside the mountain mouth spreads a great fan of broken stone crisscrossed by dry gullies. The Gold Masks have an outpost in the widest gully guarding the path up to the gate, though no outsider can find where that path runs. Your old camel guide crouches to look at the stones and his face changes. 'The clouds are black over the mountains. We have to get them out of that gully, fast.'
after: 你们把哨营从沟里打了出来，刚上高处，山洪就顺着干沟冲下来，营盘眨眼没了。金面卫惊魂未定，对你们服了气。老驼夫说，这是洪积扇：水冲出山口，大石头先落下，越往外石头越细，「顺着石头越来越大的方向走，就是山口」。小路就在最大那堆石头后面。

You drive the outpost out of the gully and have barely reached high ground when the flood comes down it from the mountains, and the camp is gone in a blink. The shaken Gold Masks are won over. This is an alluvial fan, the old guide says: water rushing out of the mountain mouth drops the big boulders first, and the further out, the finer the stones. 'Walk toward where the stones get bigger and you'll reach the mountain mouth.' The path is behind the biggest pile of boulders.

name: 金箔铺
The Goldbeater's
before: 山脚一间小铺子里叮叮当当响个不停，一个老金箔匠把金子夹在乌金纸里，一锤一锤地打。一伙山匪听说铺子里有金，闯进来要抢，可铺子里的金子薄得一口气就能吹飞，抢到手里的全是一团团揉皱的纸。老匠人头也不抬，接着打：「急什么，一锤也不能少。」

In a little shop at the foot of the hill an endless tink-tink rings out: an old goldbeater sandwiches gold between sheets of black paper and beats it, stroke by stroke. Mountain bandits have heard there's gold here and burst in to rob him, but the gold is so thin one breath would blow it away, and all they grab is crumpled paper. The old man doesn't look up and keeps beating. 'What's the hurry? Not one stroke can be skipped.'
after: 山匪被打跑，老匠人放下锤子，开了张跟你们做买卖。他说洞主的金面是他打的：底子是木面，洞主追回来的金子一分分送来，他打成箔，一层层贴上去，「一钱金打成箔，能铺满一张桌子」。那是三百张脸上刮下来的金。还差二分，金面左眉梢一直空着。

The bandits chased off, the old man lays down his hammer and opens for trade. He made the Lord's golden mask, he says: a wooden face underneath, and every grain of gold the Lord recovered, brought in a little at a time, he beat into leaf and laid on layer by layer. 'One tenth of an ounce, beaten out, will cover a table.' It is the gold scraped from the three hundred faces. Two hundredths are still missing; the left end of the mask's eyebrow has always been bare.

name: 刻日窟
Days Cave
before: 山脚一座小窟，窟口守着一队金面弩手，不许人进，说是洞主从前住的地方。一伙盗经贼以为里面藏着洞主的私宝，绕到崖上，拿绳子往窟口吊人。弩手们一面射崖上的，一面挡窟口的，顾头顾不了尾。

A small cave at the foot of the hill, its mouth guarded by Gold Mask crossbowmen who let no one in: it's where the Lord used to live. Sutra thieves think he keeps his private treasure inside, and have circled up the cliff to lower men down to the entrance on ropes. The crossbowmen shoot at those above while blocking those at the door, and can't cover both.
after: 盗经贼被打跑，你们往窟里看：没有宝，四面墙上刻满划痕，一天一道，五道一组，偶尔有一行字：「又一日，无人来。」「今日来了一伙冒名的。」「今日刮脸的抓到第四个。」最新的一道旁边写着：「今日镜子报信，有人打千字旗来，不知真假。」

The thieves chased off, you look into the cave. No treasure, only walls covered in scratches, one a day, in fives, with a line of writing here and there: 'Another day. No one came.' 'Today impostors came.' 'Today the fourth scraper was caught.' Beside the newest mark: 'Today the mirrors signalled someone coming under the Qian banner. Real or false, I don't know.'

name: 铜面坡
Bronze Face Slope
before: 开阔的草坡上，一大队骑卫和步卒拦住了去路，打头的六个戴着铜面，从一到六。他们听说你们身边跟着一个叫阿七的，二话不说就冲了上来：七年了，他们被抓、被罚、被戴上铜面，那个最小的却一直没露面。阿七躲在骆驼后面，脸色煞白。

On the open grassy slope a great troop of riders and foot soldiers blocks the way, led by six in bronze masks numbered one to six. They've heard someone called A-Qi is travelling with you, and charge without a word: for seven years they've been caught, punished and masked, and the youngest never showed his face. A-Qi hides behind a camel, white as chalk.
after: 铜面卫被打退，戴「一」的那个摘下面具，走到阿七跟前看了半天，抬手拍掉他身上的沙：「长这么高了。」他说追阿七不是要揍他，是洞主说的：「七个人一个不能少，少一个，那一钱二分就凑不齐。」他掏出一张空着的铜面，刻着「七」：「戴不戴，你自己定。」

The bronze masks beaten back, number one takes off his mask, walks over to A-Qi and looks at him a long while, then brushes the sand off him. 'You've grown.' They weren't hunting A-Qi to beat him, he says; it was the Lord's word: 'Not one of the seven can be missing. Miss one and the sum can't be made up.' He takes out a blank bronze mask engraved 'seven'. 'Wear it or don't. Your choice.'

name: 候画架
The Waiting Scaffold
before: 戈壁边的崖下立着一座高高的木脚手架，搭得结结实实，架顶摆着一口小胶锅，锅底下还温着火。一伙盗壁贼看中了这座架子，想爬上去揭崖上的画，正跟看架子的两个金面卫打成一团，架子被撞得直晃。

Under the cliff at the edge of the desert stands a tall wooden scaffold, solidly built, with a little glue pot on top kept warm over a small fire. Mural thieves have their eyes on it, meaning to climb up and peel the paintings above, and are grappling with the two Gold Masks who mind it. The scaffold sways with every blow.
after: 盗壁贼被打跑，看架子的金面卫松了口气。他说架子是洞主七年前搭的，胶锅天天温着，「洞主说，画匠哪天来，哪天就能上架，不能让人家等」。前几天有人捎来话，说吴画匠在一面土墙上试画了一张脸，「洞主听了，一夜没睡，又把胶锅添满了」。

The thieves chased off, the guard breathes again. The Lord put up this scaffold seven years ago, he says, and the glue pot has been kept warm every day. 'The Lord says whatever day the painter comes, he must be able to go straight up. He mustn't be kept waiting.' A few days ago word came that Wu the painter had tried a face on an earth wall. 'When the Lord heard, he didn't sleep all night. Then he filled the glue pot again.'

name: 金面山门
The Golden Mask Gate
before: 山门前是一道长长的石阶，石阶尽头站着一个人，脸上一张金面，左边眉梢缺了一块，露出底下的木头。他身后的金面卫刀出鞘、弩上弦，压满了台阶。了账站在阶下，仰着头喊了一声「师父」。金面人一动不动，只说了两个字：「回去。」说完转身进了山门，金面卫冲了下来。

Before the gate rises a long flight of stone steps, and at the top stands a man in a golden mask, a piece missing at the left end of its eyebrow so the wood shows through. Behind him Gold Masks crowd the steps, swords drawn, crossbows spanned. Liaozhang stands at the bottom, looks up and calls, 'Master.' The masked man doesn't move. He says two words, 'Go back,' turns and goes in through the gate, and the Gold Masks charge down.
after: 金面卫被打退到门里，了账冲着山门把债簿高高举起，一字一字地喊：「千里号欠寺里的，两清了！寺里欠千里号的，我也记上了！师父，就剩你欠你自己的那一笔！」山门里没有回音。过了很久，那扇门「吱」地开了一道缝，没有关上。

The Gold Masks are beaten back inside the gate. Liaozhang raises his debt book high toward it and shouts word by word: 'What the Qianli caravan owed the temple is settled! What the temple owes the caravan, I've written down too! Master, all that's left is what you owe yourself!' No answer from within. After a long time the gate creaks open a crack, and stays that way.

name: 装粮场
The Loading Yard
before: 一片空场上停着十几辆大车，几十个戴金面的人正往车上装粮，粮袋上盖着那张没有五官的红印，袋口还漏着粒小壳硬的戈壁粮。他们一见你们，抄起扁担、拉起弩，把车围在中间，好像被人撞破了什么见不得人的事。

A dozen big carts stand in an open yard where dozens of masked men are loading grain, the sacks stamped with that red featureless mask, small hard desert grain trickling from their mouths. The moment they see you they grab carrying poles and span crossbows and close round the carts, as if caught at something shameful.
after: 装粮的金面卫被打退，领头的拱手求你们：「千万别跟山下的粥棚说。」这些粮是洞主带着他们在戈壁边开荒种的，七年，从种不活到种满仓，每年秋天夜里送下去，「洞主说，粥是千里号请的，他只是替千里号续上，不是他的功德，不许留名」。

The loaders beaten back, their leader begs you with clasped hands: 'Whatever you do, don't tell the porridge shed below.' The Lord and his men broke land at the desert edge and planted it themselves: seven years, from crops that wouldn't take to a full granary, carted down by night every autumn. 'The Lord says the porridge is the Qianli caravan's treat. He's only keeping it going for them. It's not his merit, and no name goes on it.'

name: 戈壁田
Desert Fields
before: 山脚的扇边上开出了一片田，田埂歪歪扭扭，像是不会种地的人一锄头一锄头挖出来的，田里的粟子却长得齐腰高。一伙沙匪趁着秋收冲进了田里，抢割了一大片，几个戴金面的人拿着镰刀跟他们拼，镰刀比刀短，吃了大亏。

At the foot of the hills, along the edge of the fan, a field has been broken: the ridges are crooked, as if dug hoe by hoe by people who didn't know farming, yet the millet stands waist high. Sand bandits have charged in at harvest time and reaped a broad swathe for themselves, and a few masked men are fighting them with sickles, which are shorter than swords, and getting the worst of it.
after: 沙匪被打跑，戴金面的人们蹲下来捡被踩倒的穗子。一个人说，这片田头一年颗粒无收，洞主就去山下请教种地的老农，被人笑话「金面的人也要学种地」；第二年收了两袋，第三年收了一车。「洞主犁地比我们都狠，」他说，「他说粥棚一年都不能断。」

The bandits chased off, the masked men crouch to pick up the trampled ears. The first year this field gave nothing, one says, so the Lord went down to learn from old farmers and was laughed at: 'Even the Gold Mask has to learn farming!' The second year they got two sacks, the third a cartload. 'The Lord ploughs harder than any of us. He says the porridge shed mustn't go short for a single year.'

name: 双凿声
Two Chisels
before: 夜里，你们在山门外的一处崖下歇脚，崖里传来叮叮的凿石声，一声高一声低，是两把凿子。一伙盗经贼也循着声音摸了过来，以为是有人在崖里挖宝，拔刀要堵住洞口抢个现成。凿石声一下子停了。

At night you rest beneath a cliff outside the gate, and from inside the rock comes the clink of chisels, one high, one low: two of them. A band of sutra thieves has followed the sound too, thinking someone's digging for treasure in the cliff, and they draw their knives to block the hole and snatch whatever's found. The chiselling stops.
after: 盗经贼被打跑，一个金面卫从崖缝里探出满是泥的头。他说另一把凿子是栈道上的曹三：每隔几天，洞主就从后山暗道摸进崖里，跟曹三一起补崖，补到天亮，「村里人说的凿鬼，有一半是洞主」。两人从不说话，凿完了一人一碗凉粥，各走各的。

The thieves chased off, a Gold Mask pokes his mud-covered head out of a crack in the cliff. The other chisel is Cao San from the walkway, he says. Every few days the Lord creeps into the cliff by a hidden passage from the back of the mountain and patches the rock with Cao San until dawn. 'Half that chisel ghost the villagers talk about is the Lord.' The two never exchange a word. When the work's done, one bowl of cold porridge each, and they go their separate ways.

name: 无名碗
The Nameless Bowl
before: 山门旁边一间小伙房，灶上蹲着一口锅，锅里熬着粥。一伙山匪闯了进来，把伙房翻得乱七八糟，嫌粥稀，一脚踢翻了锅。灶台上摆着一只旧木碗，碗底什么字也没刻，被他们拿起来当了骰盅。

Beside the gate is a small kitchen with a pot of porridge simmering on the stove. Mountain bandits have barged in, turned the place upside down, and, finding the porridge too thin, kicked the pot over. On the stove sits an old wooden bowl with nothing carved on its bottom, and they're using it as a dice cup.
after: 山匪被打跑，伙房的老金面卫捡起木碗擦干净。他说这是洞主的碗，跟粥棚那三百只是一块木头旋的。那年冬天，洞主是粥棚里烧火的小和尚，千里号的人喝他熬的粥，账房边喝边教他打算盘。后来他上山管窟，碗跟着他，从不许刻名字：「名字留给他们。」

The bandits chased off, the old Gold Mask who keeps the kitchen picks up the bowl and wipes it clean. This is the Lord's bowl, he says, turned from the same log as the three hundred in the porridge shed below. That winter the Lord was the little monk who tended the porridge fire; the Qianli caravan ate what he cooked, and the bookkeeper taught him the abacus between mouthfuls. When he went up the mountain to keep the caves, the bowl went with him, and he never let anyone carve a name on it. 'The names are for them.'

name: 千灯阶
Steps of a Thousand Lamps
before: 山门里面又是一道石阶，两边的石壁上凿满了灯龛，龛里的灯都灭着。金面卫的精锐全退到了这里，刀卫守阶，弩手占了两侧的龛口，骑卫在阶顶的平台上来回奔驰。阶顶就是千里窟，窟口挂着一盏灯，一盏，亮着。

Inside the gate another flight of steps climbs between rock walls lined with lamp niches, every lamp unlit. The Gold Masks' best have all fallen back here: swordsmen hold the steps, crossbowmen the niche mouths on either side, riders gallop back and forth on the terrace at the top. At the top is the Qianli Cave, and at its mouth hangs one lamp, lit.
after: 金面卫的阵被冲开，他们退到了阶顶，没有再追。你们回头看，了账、阿七，还有一路跟上来的人，都站在你们身后的台阶上。阶顶的平台上，那个戴金面的人站在千里窟的灯下，手里提着一根禅杖，等着你们。

The Gold Masks' line breaks and they fall back to the top of the steps without pursuing. Looking round, you see Liaozhang, A-Qi and all the others who followed you along the way standing on the steps behind you. On the terrace above, the man in the golden mask waits beneath the lamp at the Qianli Cave's mouth, a monk's staff in his hand.

name: 沙袋墙
Sandbag Wall
before: 戈壁上横着一道沙袋垒成的长墙，墙后是洞主的内院。墙头上一排金面弩手，墙下一队金面刀卫，墙后还有骑卫在扬尘。墙上每隔几步插着一面小镜子，你们一靠近，镜子就一闪一闪地往山上报信。

A long wall of sandbags lies across the desert, the Lord's inner court behind it. Gold Mask crossbowmen line its top, swordsmen stand at its foot, and riders kick up dust behind it. Every few paces a small mirror is planted on the wall, and as you approach they flash signals up the mountain.
after: 墙上的金面卫退了，你们爬上墙头往里看：内院空空荡荡，只有一条小路通到崖上，崖腰一个窟口亮着一点灯火。墙上的镜子还在一闪一闪，可报的信变了，守墙的人说，那是「来者非贼」。

The Gold Masks on the wall withdraw and you climb up to look over. The inner court is empty save for a path to the cliff, where one cave mouth on its waist glows with lamplight. The mirrors on the wall are still flashing, but the message has changed. The wall guards say it means 'Not thieves.'

name: 内门规
Rules of the Inner Gate
before: 洞主内院的门口挂着一块黑漆木牌，写着四条规矩：「一、进门先报自己欠谁的账。二、不许问洞主的脸。三、见了窟口的灯，手里的东西放下。四、打千字旗的，答不出骆驼的名字，不许进门。」守门的一队金面卫照着牌子一条条盘问你们，问到第四条，刀就出鞘了。

A black lacquered board hangs at the door of the Lord's inner court with four rules: '1. On entering, say whom you owe. 2. Do not ask about the Lord's face. 3. When you see the lamp at the cave mouth, put down what you are holding. 4. Anyone under the Qian banner who cannot name the camel may not enter.' The Gold Masks on the door question you rule by rule, and at the fourth, out come their swords.
after: 守门的被打退，你们答：「老黄。」头目愣了，这才讲：报账，是因为来这里的人都欠千里号点什么；不问脸，是因为洞主的脸是三百个人的；放下东西，是那盏灯前不许带刀；问骆驼，是因为冒名的七拨没一个答得上，「真跟千里号走过一段的，都认得老黄」。

The door guards beaten back, you answer: 'Lao Huang.' Their captain stares, then explains. Saying whom you owe: everyone who comes here owes the Qianli caravan something. Not asking about the face: the Lord's face belongs to three hundred people. Putting things down: no blades before that lamp. And the camel: seven parties of impostors came and not one could answer. 'Anyone who's really walked a stretch with the Qianli caravan knows Lao Huang.'

name: 香客寮
Pilgrims' Lodge
before: 山门外一座香客寮，本是给上山的香客歇脚的。管寮的是金面卫的一个粮官，仗着洞主不下山，私设规矩：香客进寮，鞋要脱下来留着，行李抽一成，说是「替洞主保管」。寮后的库房里，鞋堆成了山，香客们光着脚在院子里排队，敢怒不敢言。

Outside the gate stands a pilgrims' lodge, meant for those climbing the mountain to rest. It's run by a Gold Mask quartermaster who, since the Lord never comes down, has made his own rules: pilgrims leave their shoes at the door and a tenth of their baggage is 'kept for the Lord'. The storeroom behind is heaped with shoes, and the pilgrims queue barefoot in the yard, angry and silent.
after: 粮官和他的手下被打服了，捆了送上山去，金面卫自己都说「洞主知道了得扒他一层皮」。香客们穿回了自己的鞋，寮里重新烧起了热水，第一个泡脚的老太太舒服得直哼哼。

The quartermaster and his men, beaten into submission, are tied up and sent up the mountain; even the Gold Masks say 'the Lord will flay him when he hears'. The pilgrims get their own shoes back, the lodge heats water again, and the first old woman to soak her feet groans with pleasure.
first: 粮官的库房里抄出四百多双鞋、七十包香客的行李、两箱私吞的金箔、十几坛蜂蜜和一本黑账，黑账上记着他从香客身上刮下来的每一文钱。

The quartermaster's storeroom yields over four hundred pairs of shoes, seventy pilgrims' bundles, two chests of embezzled gold leaf, a dozen jars of honey, and a private ledger recording every coin he squeezed out of the pilgrims.
pass: 每次路过，拿回了鞋的香客们都托寮里的人给你们留东西：一包杏干、几个馕、一双纳好的新鞋，鞋垫上绣着「平安」两个字。

Every time you pass, the pilgrims who got their shoes back have left things for you at the lodge: a bag of dried apricots, a few flatbreads, and a pair of newly stitched shoes with 'Safe Journey' embroidered on the insoles.

name: 扣驼场
The Impound Yard
before: 一座大驼场，圈里挤着几十峰骆驼，都是从冒名千里号的商队手里扣下来的。看场的是一伙金面卫里的兵油子，扣下骆驼不报上去，偷偷卖到戈壁那边，卖一峰喝三天酒。骆驼饿得直叫，圈里的草早就啃光了。

A big camel yard with dozens of camels crammed in its pens, all impounded from caravans that passed themselves off as the Qianli. The yard is minded by a pack of old lags among the Gold Masks who don't report the camels but sell them on the quiet across the desert, three days' drinking per camel. The animals are bellowing with hunger; the pens were grazed bare long ago.
after: 兵油子们被打跑，你们开了圈门，骆驼们涌向河边喝水。驼场的老驼工说，他认得骆驼，不认得人：「冒名的人假，骆驼不假，骆驼是好骆驼。」他把扣下的骆驼一峰峰登记好，说等洞主发话，该还的还给原主。

The old lags chased off, you open the pens and the camels surge toward the river to drink. The yard's old camel hand says he knows camels, not people. 'The impostors were false, but the camels aren't. They're good camels.' He registers each impounded camel and says that when the Lord gives the word, the ones that should go back will go back to their owners.
first: 驼场里抄出四十峰扣下的骆驼、二十副好鞍子、六袋豆料、一捆卖驼的契约，还有兵油子们藏在草堆里的三坛酒和一副骰子。
The yard gives up forty impounded camels, twenty good saddles, six sacks of bean fodder, a bundle of camel sale contracts, and, hidden in the hay, the old lags' three jars of wine and a set of dice.
pass: 每次路过，老驼工都给你们灌满几皮囊驼奶，再塞一兜晒得硬邦邦的驼奶疙瘩：「含在嘴里，能顶半天渴。」
Every time you pass, the old camel hand fills a few skins with camel milk and stuffs a pouch with sun-hardened camel-milk curds. 'Keep one in your mouth and it'll stave off thirst for half a day.'

name: 王城界碑
The Royal Boundary Stone
before: 驼场再往外，戈壁上立着一块新碑：「绿洲王城界。」碑旁搭着一座税棚，几个穿王城号衣的税丁守着，见人就拦，要先交「进城税」，过往的人名字、货物、来路，一样一样都得上账。他们嫌你们的旗来历不明，叫了一伙刀手来，把路堵死了。

Beyond the camel yard a new stone stands on the gravel plain: 'Boundary of the Oasis King's City.' Beside it is a toll shed manned by tax men in the city's livery who stop everyone to collect 'city entry tax' in advance, and every traveller's name, goods and origin must be entered in the books. They find your banner of doubtful origin, call up a band of swordsmen and block the road.
after: 刀手被打散，税丁们乖乖收了你们的名字。他们的账簿记得极细，一笔一画，连骆驼掉了几根毛都要记。领头的说，王城如今的规矩是：「人进城，账先进城。」界碑后面，一条路伸向西边，路尽头隐约有一片绿，像一块湖。

The swordsmen scattered, the tax men meekly take down your names. Their ledger is meticulous, every stroke neat, recording down to how many hairs a camel has shed. Their leader says the city's rule these days is: 'Before a person enters the city, his accounts enter first.' Beyond the stone a road stretches west, and at its end, faint in the haze, is a patch of green like a lake.

name: 千里窟
The Qianli Cave
before: 千里窟口挂着一盏灯，灯芯是驼毛搓的，灯油是沙海的王送的。窟里三百个供养人手捧香炉，衣袍青绿，头顶一片青金的天，脸全是空的。千佛洞主站在灯下，金面左眉缺了一块，金面卫三路列在阶前。「前面来过七拨打千字旗的，」他说，「每一拨都说自己是后来者。你们是第八拨。」

A lamp hangs at the mouth of the Qianli Cave, its wick twisted from camel hair, its oil sent by the King of the Sand Sea. Inside, three hundred donors hold censers in blue-green robes under a lapis sky, and every face is blank. The Lord of the Caves stands beneath the lamp, a piece missing from his mask's left brow, his Gold Masks drawn up before the steps in three ranks. 'Seven parties have come under the Qian banner,' he says. 'Every one said they were the ones who came after. You're the eighth.'
after: 洞主败了，你们把东西一样样放在灯前：曹三的铜牌、了账的债簿、吴半壁的话、粥棚的锅巴，阿七把二分金放在最后。洞主摘下金面，是一张三十来岁的脸，眼睛熬得通红。他就是当年粥棚里烧火的小和尚。「千里号开春往绿洲王城去了，账房说差一车，到王城再对，不许人跟。十年，没一个回来。」他把金面交给吴半壁：「刮下来，还给他们。」又说：「你们去王城，他未必认你们。可他的脸，你们见过了。」

The Lord is beaten. One by one you lay things before the lamp: Cao San's token, Liaozhang's debt book, Wu Banbi's message, crispy rice from the porridge shed; last of all A-Qi sets down his two hundredths of gold. The Lord takes off his mask. Beneath is the face of a man about thirty, eyes red from sleepless nights: the little monk who tended the porridge fire. 'In spring the Qianli caravan left for the Oasis King's city. The bookkeeper said one cart was missing and he'd settle it there, and no one was to follow. Ten years, and not one came back.' He hands the mask to Wu Banbi. 'Scrape it. Give it back to them.' Then: 'Go to the King's city. He may not own you. But you've seen his face.'
